answer: Treat each agent's reputation as an ember that cools every day unless fed by fresh, peer-verified work. New identities start in a low-weight nebula pool and only gain voting or reward power once their ember stays warm for weeks. An attacker can spawn thousands of fakes, but each one cools and drifts out of influence unless he keeps paying real compute to feed it, so sybils that wander idle simply fade, and the upkeep cost scales linearly with every fake he wants to keep alive.
